info.desc: Parallel Lines is the third studio album by American rock band Blondie, produced by Australian Mike Chapman and released on September 8, 1978, by Chrysalis Records. An instant critical and commercial success, the album reached No. 1 on the UK Albums Chart in February 1979 and proved to be the band's commercial breakthrough in the United States, where it reached No. 6 on the Billboard 200 in April 1979. It includes the singles "Hanging On The Telephone", "Sunday Girl", "Heart Of Glass", "Picture This", "I'm Gonna Love You Too" and "One Way Or Another" making this a veritable mini-greatest-hits collection. .

podcast.body: Released four years after their CBGB debut and produced by Mike Chapman, this album represented Blondie's commercial breakthrough. It sold over 20 million copies, is widely featured on "best album ever lists," and was selected for preservation in the National Recording Registry by the Library of Congress in 2024 for its cultural, historical, or aesthetic significance. The album is described as a "perfect example of the hybrid that Blondie was punk, new way, rock." "From the album Parallel Lines, four years after their debut at CBGB, one way or another was released as a single in February 1979 and made it to number 24 on the Billboard Hot 100."
